improvedVsOld: Clearly better overall. The new text removes the English left in the old version (campgrounds, caravan parks in the image alt texts), fixes the app labels to match the app (Me gustó, Quiero visitar, Pines, Todos guardados instead of Me gusta, Quiero ir, Marcadores), drops the banned 'parque vacacional' and the vosotros form ('estáis discutiendo'), uses the glossary terms 'zona de acampada gratuita' and 'acampada libre', and adopts the style guide's before/after rewrites (featureMainTitle, plannerText, principle2Title). A few units regressed against the old text: toolsTitle ('cuentas misteriosas'), support.sections[3].heading (the 'tiempo / tiempo real' clash) and toolsReadingText. The 14 units scoring below 4 are wording fixes, not systematic problems.
criticalIssues: Pre-existing gap, not introduced by this diff, but this branch rewrites the privacy page and leaves it out of step with English. The Spanish file has no consent.* keys (label, message, accept, decline, learnMore, privacyChoices) and no 'Website analytics' (GA4) privacy section. origin/main en.json has 7 privacy sections and es.json has 6, so from index 4 the sections are off by one (es[4] 'Conservación y control' sits where EN[4] is 'Website analytics'). The Spanish privacy page therefore does not disclose GA4 or its cookies, even though GA4 and the consent banner are now live. Add them before or alongside this merge.

No em dashes, no 'offline map' claims, no vosotros/usted, no untranslated English and no broken placeholders or markup were found in the changed units. Numbers (74.000), AUD and app labels (Me gustó, Quiero visitar, Pines, Todos guardados, Mirar alrededor) follow the style guide.

Out of scope for this diff (article bodies were not changed): es.json still uses 'autosuficiente' as the main term 8 times, against the glossary's 'self-contained', and uses 'céntimos' twice (articles.public-transport-costs-australia-2026), which should be 'centavos'. The 'mapas sin conexión' hits in articles are about downloading third-party maps, not claims about the app, so they are acceptable.
